meetups.title: AWS Meetup Vienna #53 - hosted by RBI
meetups.summary: Autumn is arriving in Vienna - and so is our next AWS meetup!
meetups.description:
Autumn is arriving in Vienna - and so is our next AWS meetup!

In this October edition, we’ll explore what AI-assisted cloud operations looks like in practice: from using AWS DevOps Agent to investigate incidents, correlate signals, and support real DevOps workflows, to building safer and more trustworthy AI agents for production. Our speakers will share hands-on lessons, real-world examples, and practical patterns for rolling out AI agents responsibly in AWS environments.

A big thank you to [Raiffeisen Bank International AG](https://www.rbinternational.com/de/raiffeisen.html) for supporting the community and making the meetup possible!

***

 **Location**
Raiffeisen Bank International
Mooslackengasse 12, 1190 Wien, Austria

 **When**
**October 20nd 2026**
Doors open at 17:00 for networking, food & drinks.
Talks start at 18:00.

***

 **Agenda**

* **17:00 - 18:00:** Entry & Networking
* **18:00 - 18:05:** Welcome and Introduction AWS Community Vienna
* **18:05 - 18:10:** Welcome and Introduction to the sponsors (**Raiffeisen Bank International**)
* **18:10 - 18:50:** **"Teaching an AI to Debug Our Cloud: AWS DevOps Agent in Practice"**
* **18:50 - 19:20:** Networking break
* **19:20 - 20:00:** **"I don't trust my agents!"**
* **20:00 - Open End:** Networking

**"Teaching an AI to Debug Our Cloud: AWS DevOps Agent in Practice"**
*Speakers:*
**[Roman Jokel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/roman-jokel/),** Cloud Architect (Raiffeisen Bank International)
**[Mladen Trampic](https://www.linkedin.com/in/trampic/)**, Senior Technical Account Manager@AWS

*About the talk:*
AWS DevOps Agent is AWS's AI-powered teammate for operations - it investigates incidents, correlates logs/metrics/traces/deployments, proposes mitigations, and learns your environment over time through custom skills and memory. In this talk, we'll walk through what it can actually do, how we rolled it out across our AWS organization, the custom skills we built to teach it our environment (networking, IAM, account provisioning, firewall logs, and more), and the real incidents it has helped us resolve. We'll close with the honest lessons learned - what worked, what surprised us, and what we'd do differently - so you can walk away with a realistic picture of what AI-assisted operations looks like in practice, not just in theory.

**"I don't trust my agents!"**
*Speaker:* [Darko Mesaroš](https://www.linkedin.com/in/darko-mesaros/) Principal Technologist@AWS

*About the talk:*
Your AI agent works great in the demo. Then you deploy it and it hallucinates a refund policy, exposes customer data, or just loops endlessly burning tokens. This session walks through a layered approach to agent safety using tools like Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK: guardrails, observability, multi-agent safety patterns, and reference architectures you can adapt immediately.

***

 **Sponsors:**

* **RBI** - [Raiffeisen Bank International AG](https://www.rbinternational.com/de/raiffeisen.html)

speakers.name: Darko Mesaroš
speakers.bio:
I am a computer person who writes Rust, breaks things on AWS, and collects computers older than most of my audience. By title I'm a Principal Developer Advocate, by practice I'm live-coding on Twitch or convincing a 1974 minicomputer to do something useful. I build CLI tools nobody asked for but everyone ends up using, blog about Rust and cloud development right here, and firmly believe the terminal is the best UI ever made. I'm happiest when a demo works on the first try, which almost never happens.

I also care deeply about developer productivity and coding assistants. I spend an unreasonable amount of time teaching AI agents to be better coding companions, building MCP servers, and automating everything that stands still long enough. If there's a way to make developers faster and happier, I'm probably already tinkering with it.

meetups.description:
Autumn is arriving in Vienna - and so is our next AWS meetup!

If you’ve ever run `terraform init`, chances are high you’ve already used his code. **Anton Babenko - AWS Community Hero**, creator of the **Terraform AWS modules** (provisioned over 2 billion times worldwide), **author** of the Terraform Best Practices ebook, and the voice behind the Your Weekly Dose of Terraform YouTube channel - is joining us live in **Vienna**.

He’ll show how to close the trust gap between AI-generated Terraform and production reality. No slides-only theory: real modules, real contracts, real guardrails, live on stage. Plus: a second speaker and topic to be announced soon - stay tuned!
A big thank you to **enspired GmbH** for hosting us and keeping the community alive!

***

 Location
enspired GmbH **Wagenseilgasse 3/4, 1120 Wien**

 When
Monday, September 28, 2026 Doors open at 17:00 for networking, food & drinks. Talks start at 18:00.

***

 Agenda
17:00 - 18:00: Entry & Networking
18:00 - 18:05: Welcome and Introduction AWS Community Vienna 18:05 - 18:10: Welcome and Introduction to the sponsors (enspired) 18:10 - 18:50: "The Terraform Trust Gap: Engineering the Space Between Prompts and Production" 18:50 - 19:20: Networking break 19:20 - 20:00: "enspired by CDK" 20:00 - Open End: Networking

***

**"The Terraform Trust Gap: Engineering the Space Between Prompts and Production"**

**Speaker: Anton Babenko - AWS Community Hero** / Terraform influencer / compliance.tf

About the talk:
Agents can already write Terraform. That was never the hard part. The hard part is that the context going in is stale and the apply coming out is too easy to hand over, so you get code that looks right, passes your linters, even `terraform plan` passed, but still it quietly does the wrong thing in production. This talk runs one module everyone knows, `terraform-aws-modules/s3-bucket`, through the whole chain live. First I give the agent a real contract instead of a README and watch the hallucinated config disappear. Then I take one of the module's own examples and turn it into a fixture that fails the moment it drifts from the module. Then I let the agent plan changes but not apply them. A human has to approve the plan first, and apply only runs on the approved one. On stage the agent tries to apply by itself and you watch it get blocked. You leave with three things to do on Monday, every pattern working with open tooling, and an honest feedback of where the chain still breaks. No vendor account, no prompt magic.

***

**"enspired by CDK"**
Speakers: [Andreas Werschlan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/andreas-werschlan-08b4462b0/), [Michal Sedlak](https://www.linkedin.com/in/michal-sedlak-137105183/) and Orlin Filev

About the talk:
Discover how we evolved our Infrastructure as Code journey with AWS CDK - from fast early implementations to standardised, reusable, production-ready patterns and secure, universal deployments. We will share the decisions, best practices, lessons learned, and hard-earned insights that helped us understand not only how to use CDK effectively, but also when not to use it.

***

 Sponsors: **enspired GmbH** - [https://www.enspired-trading.com/](https://www.enspired-trading.com/)
Founded in 2020 to solve the biggest challenges in the energy industry, enspired has been pushing the boundaries of innovation since day one. Driven by the belief that technology will make the energy transition a reality, we developed a state-of-the-art optimization platform in the early days of algo trading to integrate the flexibility we need for an efficient and sustainable energy system.

***

meetups.title: AWS User Group Vienna presents: Agentic Football Cup 2026
meetups.summary: The football summer may be over, but the next tournament is just kicking off - and this time, the teams are powered by AI.
meetups.description:
**The football summer may be over, but the next tournament is just kicking off - and this time, the teams are powered by AI.**

Join **AWS User Group Vienna** for a special **Agentic Football Cup** edition hosted by us at the real football **Generali Arena** stadion: a hands-on workshop where you will build a team of autonomous AI agents, send them onto a virtual football pitch, and compete against other teams.

Strategy, teamwork, rapid decisions and the pressure of match day are not just football concepts.
They are also the foundations of effective multi-agent systems. Build your squad, refine its tactics, deploy it to AWS, and see whether your agents have what it takes to lift the cup. This is a great opportunity to develop a better understanding of the agents on AWS via exciting football sessions!

A huge thank you to **DoIT** for sponsoring and hosting this special event at the Generali Arena!

***

 **Location**
Generali Arena
Horrplatz 1, 1100 Wien

 **When**
**Tuesday, 25 August 2026**
Doors open at **16:00** for registration, food and networking.
Workshop starts at **16:30**.

***

## Agenda

16:00 - 16:30: Entry, registration & team forming
16:30 - 16:35: Welcome and introduction - AWS User Group Vienna
16:35 - 16:40: Welcome from our sponsor, DoIT
16:40 - 17:00: Kick-off: Agentic Football Cup Introduction & Workshop Setup
17:00 - 17:40: Workshop - build and deploy your Agentic Football Team
17:40 - 18:40: Fine tune your agents & Practice Matches
18:40 - 19:25: Tournament
19:25 - 20:00: Winners Ceremony, networking, food & drinks

***

## Agentic Football Cup

The [Agentic Football Cup](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/pjphorn_im-really-pleased-to-announce-that-the-aws-activity-7465345891458011136-MQ9u) is a free, hands-on AWS workshop where you build a five-agent football team, deploy it on AWS, and watch it compete in live 5v5 matches. Each agent receives the live game state, makes an independent decision, and acts on the pitch alongside its teammates.

Behind the football theme are real-world patterns for building agentic applications: multi-agent orchestration, structured outputs, tool use, latency management, observability and repeatable evaluation. The agents run on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and use foundation models to decide their [next moves during the game](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/pjphorn_im-really-pleased-to-announce-that-the-aws-activity-7465345891458011136-MQ9u).

## What to expect

* Build a team of autonomous AI football agents
* Define tactics, team roles and agent behavior
* Learn how multi-agent systems coordinate in a fast-moving environment
* Deploy and iterate on AWS
* Watch your team compete live against other participants
* Meet fellow cloud and AI builders from the Vienna community

No football or AI experience is required - just curiosity, a laptop and the desire to build something that competes.

***

 **Sponsor & Host**

**DoIT** - thank you for supporting the AWS community and making this event possible at the Generali Arena.

**"Building Conversational Agents in Code with AWS Lambda Durable Functions"**

*Speaker:* **[Gunnar Grosch](https://www.linkedin.com/in/gunnargrosch/)**\, Developer Advocate at Sinch \| ex\-AWS \| AWS Serverless Hero

*About the talk:*
Building agentic AI workflows typically requires Step Functions or complex database state machines to handle human delays. AWS Lambda Durable Functions change that. You write sequential code in a single Lambda function that can suspend for days and resume instantly, and you only pay for active compute time. In this session, we will orchestrate Amazon Bedrock conversational agents using the Sinch Conversation API to handle inbound interactions. You will learn how to dispatch AI specialists, use simple callbacks to wait for asynchronous human input, and replace heavy infrastructure boilerplate with native durable execution.

**"How RBI is automating its cloud foundation with AWS Step Functions"**
*Speaker:* **[Roman Jokel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/roman-jokel/),** Cloud Architect (Raiffeisen Informatik)
**/ [Florian Ettinger](https://www.linkedin.com/in/florian-ettinger/),** Solution Architect (AWS)

*About the talk:*
How can AWS Step Functions transform daily cloud operations? Join us to explore how RBI is using workflow orchestration to automate its cloud foundation. We’ll share practical insights from our Cloud Center of Excellence, demonstrating how Step Functions power landing zone operations, simplify automation, speed up deployments and enable scalable cloud governance across the organization.

*Speaker:* **Alexander Matev**, CISO at Bytesource

*About the talk:*
Sales CoPilot as a solution that helps teams turn complex technical customer inquiries into clear, accurate quotations much faster, reducing turnaround from hours to minutes.

The business problem: technical sales requests are slow, difficult, and error-prone when handled manually.

The Solution: Our Sales CoPilot interprets complex requirements, works with documentation and technical data, and supports offer preparation.

Technology foundation: strong emphasis on AWS as the enabler, plus AI/LLM-driven processing.
Architecture choice: a set of core AWS services to deliver both the user-facing application and the AI-powered data processing pipeline. Amazon S3 stores uploaded product datasheets and hosts the frontend assets, while Amazon CloudFront accelerates and securely delivers the web interface to users.
Incoming application traffic is routed through an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to containerized services running on Amazon ECS, which handle both backend business logic and document ingestion tasks.
For AI capabilities, Amazon Bedrock is used in two places: to extract and transform structured information from PDF datasheets, and to power the agentic logic behind the application.
Persistent structured data is stored in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, which supports read/write operations from the backend.
Together, these AWS services provide a scalable, cloud-native architecture for hosting, processing, AI enrichment, and application delivery.

###

**"Beyond Vibe Coding"**

*Speaker:* **Sergio Lopez-Gehler**, Solutions Architect @ AWS

AI agents are changing how engineers write, test, and ship code. This talk explores what agentic coding looks like in practice - the workflow, the tradeoffs, and the tools that make it work.

We'll cover how to collaborate effectively with AI agents: prompting, reviewing, iterating, and knowing when to take over. We'll look at what changes when development gets significantly faster - testing strategies, CI/CD pipelines, and team coordination all need to keep up. Then we'll introduce Kiro, an agentic IDE that uses spec-driven development, steering rules, and hooks to let engineers define how the agent operates within their codebase. We'll also look at AWS DevOps Agent - an autonomous operations teammate that correlates metrics, logs, and deployment history to investigate incidents and identify root causes before you even open your laptop.

***

* **Bytesource** - [https://bytesource.net/de/](https://bytesource.net/de/)

meetups.description:
Welcome to our next **on site** meetup!

**AWS Community GameDay Europe is coming to Vienna!**
We will join \~56 User Groups across Europe for a unique event: an international, synchronized AWS Community GameDay, powered by the European AWS community.

Join us for an intense evening combining learning, collaboration, and competition - get hands-on with AI, security and cloud-native challenges - no slides, no tutorials.

This large-scale, synchronized event is a unique opportunity to test your AWS skills in a fun, engaging, and hands-on environment.
Come with a friend, a team, or solo - we'll form teams of 2 to 4 people on site.

**What is an AWS GameDay?** A gamified learning event where participants are challenged to use AWS solutions to solve real-world technical problems as a team. Unlike traditional workshops, GameDays are open-ended and non-prescriptive, giving participants the freedom to explore and think outside the box.

** Practical information**

* Teams: 2 to 4 players - come with your team or we'll form one on site
* Equipment: Your trusty laptop (internet connection provided)
* Food & drinks: Snacks, beverages, and pizza
* AWS account: Provided on site, no personal account required
* Game duration: Around 2 hours of competition between local and international teams
* Timing: This is a synchronized international event connected via a shared live stream across all participating locations. To ensure a smooth experience, the GameDay will start on time.

** Who is this for?** The event is open to anyone with a general knowledge of AWS - no expert level required!

meetups.summary: This special joint meetup between AWS Community Vienna and Java User Group Vienna brings together two powerful technology ecosystems through the expertise of Vadym Kazulkin.
meetups.description:
**THE ULTIMATE JAVA + AWS EXPERIENCE!**

**Entry: 18:00**
**Start: 18:30**

This special joint meetup between AWS Community Vienna and [Java User Group Vienna ](https://www.meetup.com/java-vienna/events/305897281/)brings together two powerful technology ecosystems through the expertise of [Vadym Kazulkin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAAZiPSIBlSWq5_scBw9BNnemeT6DIVISHCg/). As an AWS Hero Vadym expertly bridges these worlds with practical insights gained from implementing serverless architectures at enterprise scale.

**IMPORTANT!** Please RSVP only at one event on meetup (here or at the Java UG)!

Doors open at 18:00 for networking and the AWS Workshop, food and drinks, and we start our talks at 18:30.

**1\. High performance Serverless Java on AWS**
by **[Vadym Kazulkin](https://sessionize.com/app/organizer/speaker/12910/6035e87f-e3a8-41ed-8b88-597c41f8330d)**, Head of Development at ip.labs
**What is the session about?**

* Java is for many years one of the most popular programming languages, but it used to have hard times in the Serverless community. Java is known for its high cold start times and high memory footprint, comparing to other programming languages like Node and Python. In this talk I'll look at the general best practices and techniques we can use to decrease memory consumption and cold start times for Java Serverless applications on AWS Lambda including GraalVM (Native Image) and AWS own offering SnapStart based on Firecracker microVM snapshot and restore and CRaC (Coordinated Restore at Checkpoint) runtime hooks. We'll also look into the SnapStart priming techniques which help us increase the Lambda performance and explore how AWS Lambda Profiler for Java can help us identify this potential. We'll also explore the impact of the SnapStart snapshot tiered low-latency cache on the cold start times.

**2\. How to develop\, run and optimize Spring Boot 3 application on AWS Lambda**
by **[Vadym Kazulkin](https://sessionize.com/app/organizer/speaker/12910/6035e87f-e3a8-41ed-8b88-597c41f8330d)**, Head of Development at ip.labs
**What is the session about?**

* This technical deep-dive explores multiple approaches for deploying Spring Boot 3 applications on AWS Lambda, comparing AWS Serverless Java Container, Lambda Web Adapter, Spring Cloud Function, and custom Docker images. The session examines critical cold start optimization techniques through GraalVM Native Image, AWS SnapStart with Firecracker microVM snapshots, and CRaC runtime hooks. You'll learn practical priming strategies for further reducing initialization times, understand the benefits of snapshot tiered caching, and gain insights into optimizing both cold and warm execution performance for production-ready Spring Boot Lambda functions.

**Who will present?**

* Vadym Kazulkin is Head of Development at ip.labs GmbH, a 100% subsidiary of the FUJIFILM Group, based in Bonn. ip.labs is the world's leading white label e-commerce software imaging company. Vadym has been involved with the Java ecosystem for over twenty years. His focus and interests currently include the design and implementation of highly scalable and available applications, Serverless and AWS Cloud. Vadym is the co-organizer of the Java User Group Bonn meetup and AWS Community Builder in the Serverless category and a frequent speaker at various Meetups and conferences.

**Agenda**

**18:00 - 18:30:** Entry & Networking
**18:30 - 18:35:** Welcome and Introduction
**18:35 - 19:15:** Making sense of AWS Serverless operations
**19:15 - 19:30:** Networking Break
**19:30 - 20:10:** Event-driven architecture patterns in highly scalable image storage solution
**20:10 - 20:15:** Thank you & Closing
**20:15 - Open End:** Networking

Welcome to our next **AWS User Group Vienna** meetup!

Doors open at 15:00 for networking and the AWS Workshop, food and drinks, and we start our talks at 18:00.

**1\. Workshop: Build near real\-time LLM\-powered features for monolithic applications \(Fully booked\, no more registrations possible\)**
by Franz Stefan, Robert Hanuschke, Viktor Vedmich, Florian Ettinger, Wolfgang Fuker and Manmohit Pal Singh from AWS

**What is the session about?**

* Ever needed to build new event-driven features for an existing black box or COTS application without access to the source code? In this workshop session, learn how to setup a data streaming pipeline with AWS DMS and AWS OpenSearch Serverless to build new event-driven features for existing applications using change data capture. Using this event stream and Amazon Bedrock, build a new feature to generate embeddings in near real time and store them in a Retrieval Augmented Generation knowledge base. Then, leveraging Amazon Bedrock and AWS Lambda, build an Al-powered chatbot that can respond with insights about live events in the legacy application.

**IMPORTANT: You must bring your laptop to participate.**

Services: Amazon Bedrock, Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS)

\*\*\*

**2\. Beyond Basics: Advanced RAG Techniques with Amazon Bedrock**
by Manuel Lindner, Senior Consultant at ByteSource

**What is the session about?**

* Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a powerful paradigm for building intelligent, context-aware AI applications. In this session, we’ll dive into advanced RAG architectures and best practices using Amazon Bedrock. Learn how to combine foundation models with vector databases, hybrid search strategies, and multi-step retrieval chains to build highly accurate and reliable GenAI solutions. Whether you’re designing internal copilots, customer-facing chatbots, or domain-specific search assistants, this talk will provide deep technical insights and real-world implementation patterns that go beyond the basics.

**Who will present?**

* Manuel is Senior Consultant at ByteSource with over 10 years of hands-on experience in designing and implementing robust cloud solutions. Over the past 1.5 years, I’ve been diving deep into the world of Generative AI, focusing on how to apply these emerging technologies in real-world and cloud-native environments. I’m passionate about building scalable, secure solutions and enjoy sharing insights that bridge innovation and practical implementation.

Welcome to our next **AWS User Group Vienna** meetup!

Doors open at 17:00 for networking, food and drinks, and we start our talks at 18:00.

\*\*\*
**Sandbox Management & Kubernetes Deployments**
\*\*\*

**1\. Managing AWS Sandboxes in your organisation with a breeze**
by Angjelo Thoma, Cloud Engineer at SQUER

**What is the session about?**

* In the dynamic world of cloud environments, managing sandbox accounts effectively is key to balancing innovation with governance. This talk will explore strategies for setting up and securing AWS sandbox accounts while enforcing policies and cost controls. Dive into the power of AWS Control Tower to set sandbox limits, ensuring a controlled yet flexible space for experimentation and development.

**Who will present?**

* Angjelo is a Cloud engineer with a strong background in DevOps operations within the Insurtech sector. Passionate about Kubernetes, he specializes in designing creative, scalable, and secure solutions for modern infrastructure challenges.
Furthermore, he hosts the Vienna Devops Meetup, as he enjoys sharing his learning with like-minded people. In his free time he snowboards and takes Maira (his dog) for walks!

\*\*\*

**2\. Zero\-Downtime Kubernetes Deployments on AWS with EKS**
by Philip Miglinci, Co-Founder at Glasskube

**What is the session about?**

* If you have ever hosted a web-application on EKS, Amazon's managed Kubernetes offering, you are most-likely familiar with the AWS Load Balancer Controller project (formerly AWS ALB Ingress Controller). If you have also upgraded that application, you might also be familiar with some requests failing to connect to your backend just when the roll out happens.
In this session we want to take a look at Kubernetes Networking, Pod Readiness Gates, Graceful Application Shutdown and Termination Delay with sidecars.

**Who will present?**

* Philip holds a Bachelor's degree in computer science and economics from the Vienna University of Technology and a Master's degree in Biomedical Engineering.
In 2024 Philip co founded Glasskube, an Open Source Developer Tooling company that maintains among other projects an Open Source Package Manager for Kubernetes with over 3.000 stars.
Before working on Glasskube, Philip helped build up the alerting infrastructure for firefighting organizations in Austria and Germany as CTO.
